A table of model coefficients that is safe to release

safe_model.Rd

A fitted model object carries its data: an lm or glm object holds the model frame, residuals and fitted values of every person, so it is never released. safe_model() returns the coefficient table instead, after checking with check_model() that the model rests on enough observations: residual degrees of freedom of at least min_df, every factor level and, for a binary outcome, both outcome classes with at least min_count observations.

Usage

safe_model(fit, config = NULL)

Arguments

fit

A fitted model with a coefficient table in summary(fit), for example from stats::lm(), stats::glm() or survival::coxph().

config

A mimic_config(); NULL uses the rules staff gave trial_run() or real_run(), see safe_output.

Value

A data frame with one row per coefficient: term, the columns of the coefficient table (estimate, std_error, statistic, p_value for lm and glm), observations (rounded number of observations) and df_residual.

Details

The function stops when a rule is broken, so nothing is written that would be sent back. A binary outcome with a small cell within a factor level gives a warning: the coefficient is then estimated from very few persons, and the checker will look at it.

See also

Other safe output: describe_output(), safe_count(), safe_summary()

Examples

fit <- lm(income ~ sex + occupation, data = fake_persons)
safe_model(fit)
